papers.title: Current Translational 3D In Vitro Models of Human Placental Tissue.
papers.abstract: Cellular models of placental tissue have the potential to recapitulate normal physiology, model disease, and facilitate therapeutic drug testing. In vivo or two-dimensional (2D) in vitro models of placental conditions have not been sufficiently representative of whole human tissue, thus have limited physiological relevance. This can be attributed to interspecies differences in placental physiology or a lack of structural complexity. In comparison, three-dimensional (3D) multicellular model systems provide a more sophisticated analogue of human placental tissue. Newer models of human placenta include 3D organoids, placenta-on-a-chip and organoid-on-a-chip, employing a range of materials and methods including pluripotent or trophoblast stem cells, microfluidics and 3D bioprinting. Accurately mimicking in vivo human tissue is crucial to the success of these translational 3D models of the placenta.In turn, a reliable representation of placental tissue architecture will allow discovery of the mechanisms underlying abnormal placental development and inform the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of pregnancy-related disorders such as preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction. Here, we provide a comprehensive critical appraisal of recent advances in 3D placental models, which aim to elucidate placental physiology, development and dysfunction. Additionally, we discuss how these platforms can accelerate the development of better monitoring and treatment strategies for pregnancy complications induced by a dysfunctional placenta.

papers.title: Analysis of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with anticubic nonlinearity in optical fiber systems via physics informed neural network (PINN)
papers.abstract: The higher order nonlinear phenomena such as the anticubic nonlinearity have a major influence on the evolution, stability and localization of optical pulses and play a significant role in the evolution of nonlinear optical waves in dispersive media. Therefore, effective numerical approaches for solving these nonlinear evolution equations are required to understand the intricate wave dynamics in optical fiber communication systems. In this work, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) architecture based on the DeepXDE library is developed to solve the non-linear Schrödinger equation with the anti-cubic nonlinearity. The proposed framework employs a fully connected neural network and directly integrates the underlying physical rules into the learning process without any meshing discretization. We explore the robustness of the proposed model using six representative initial conditions such as hyperbolic tangent, sine, cosine, Gaussian, super-Gaussian and hyperbolic secant profiles and study the effect of inverse nonlinear interaction parameter 𝑏 1 on the wave dynamics systematically. The numerical results show that the proposed PINN can well capture the spatiotemporal evolution of confined and periodic nonlinear wave structures. Contour and 3D surface graphs exhibit the effect of 𝑏 1 on the localization of the wave and its amplitude modulation. The numerical findings show that, the proposed PINN effectively captures the spatiotemporal evolution of constrained periodic nonlinear wave structures. Graphs of contours and three-dimensional surfaces reveal how 𝑏 1 affects the localization and amplitude modulation of the wave. The broad generalizability and steady learning tendency of the recommended framework are supported by consistent outcomes from the convergence experiment. An additional validation of the PINN prediction was conducted independently, employing the identical parameters, computational domain, governing equation, and boundary conditions as a conventional finite-difference (FD) numerical solution for a standard Gaussian initial condition. Since the PINN and FD intensity profiles agree well at 𝑡 = 2 , there is more evidence that the proposed framework is trustworthy. The results demonstrate that the proposed PINN is an effective and robust mesh-free computing approach for nonlinear wave development, and it finds applications in nonlinear optics, optical fiber communication, and other nonlinear systems.

papers.title: A physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for inverse mixed contact-traction tire-load reconstruction and finite-layer pavement response
papers.abstract: Tire-pavement interaction produces a spatially heterogeneous boundary traction that cannot be fully represented by uniform vertical pressure, particularly when braking, driving, or lateral slip generates appreciable tangential loading. Existing layered pavement models mainly address forward response prediction and provide limited capability for reconstructing unknown contact tractions and mechanically admissible transient subsurface fields from sparse observations. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for inverse tire-contact traction reconstruction and dynamic finite-layer pavement response. The tire footprint is represented by a total normal contact pressure and longitudinal and lateral traction components, without imposing a mechanically unidentifiable decomposition of the normal pressure. A three-dimensional transient finite-element reference model provides mechanics-consistent displacement, stress, strain, reaction, and strain-energy fields under a time-dependent moving load. These fields are coupled with neural reconstruction through dynamic equilibrium, constitutive, boundary, interface, force-closure, initial-condition, and regularization constraints. Source realizations are partitioned before training, and held-out contact fields are reconstructed from sparse displacement and stress histories without including their prescribed source values in the inverse loss. The framework therefore provides a unified differentiable setting for contact-traction identification, transient pavement-response reconstruction, source-disjoint evaluation, stability assessment, domain transfer, and robustness analysis.

papers.title: Revealing melt pool dynamics and mechanisms of powder spattering in laser powder bed fusion of nickel-based superalloy by in-situ high-speed synchrotron and optical imaging
papers.abstract: Spatter formation during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process of nickel-based superalloys detrimentally affects the processing reliability and consequently impacts part quality through defects and powder bed contamination. However, due to high-Z characteristics of superalloys, directly observing melt pool dynamics and related mechanisms of powder spattering and evolution remains challenging and less understood. This study presents a comprehensive in-situ investigation into powder spattering down to melt pool scale during LPBF of nickel-based GH4169 superalloy under various processing parameters by utilizing high-energy high-speed synchrotron X-ray imaging and high-speed optical imaging. Four distinct stages of droplet formation, void formation, molten liquid fluctuation and stabilization are revealed during melt pool formation process and periodic forming and wetting behavior of large droplets are characterized in subsequent stable stage. Five types of spattering formation associated with laser-irradiated dominant forces are established: gas-flow entrainment from distal powder bed region, gas-flow entrainment from proximal powder bed region, droplet separation from melt pool, direct acceleration by vapor plume, and initial gas-flow entrainment followed by vapor-plume acceleration. The spattering characteristics are profoundly dependent on keyhole fluctuation by tailoring processing parameters of laser power and scan speed. The periodic vortices in front of and behind the laser beam are experimentally captured and quantitatively characterized, arising from the entrainment effect of the ejecting vapor plume. These findings establish critical relationships between processing parameters and spattering dynamics, provide in-depth insights into the mechanisms of spattering formation and evolution, and offer effective guidance for spatter suppression and process optimization related to melt pool dynamics during the LPBF process of superalloys.

papers.title: Sling-based strength training improves functional recovery in older patients after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background Sling exercises are highly effective for strengthening core muscles and improving neuromuscular control while reducing joint strain. However, few studies have investigated the clinical effects of sling exercises on patients initiated up to 8 weeks after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Purpose This study was undertaken to investigate the effect of sling exercise on the functional recovery of patients after THA. Methods The observer-blinded trial was conducted on thirty older patients (≥ 65 years old) who had undergone THA. Participants were randomly and equally assigned to an experimental group (sling exercise program) or a comparison group (general exercise program). All participants received 30 min of comprehensive physiotherapy (5×/week for 4 weeks). In addition, the experimental group received sling exercises, and the comparison group received general exercises (5×/week for 4 weeks). Primary (stride lengths, stride times, stance times, and walking velocities) and secondary (pain scores and hip joint function scores) outcomes were measured before and after the 4-week training period. Results The experimental group achieved greater increases in stride length and walking velocity than the comparison group (stride length, +19.5 vs. + 10.3 cm, p < .008, 2 = .880; walking velocity, +11.7 vs. + 8 cm/s, p < .016, 2 = .274, respectively). However, changes in stride times, stance times, pain scores, and hip joint function scores after intervention were similar in the two groups. Conclusion Sling-based strengthening exercise may improve walking function recovery more than general exercise in older patients after total hip arthroplasty.

papers.title: Long-term outcomes of resurfacing total hip arthroplasty in young active patients: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Resurfacing Total Hip Arthroplasty (R-THA) provides a bone-conserving alternative to Conventional Total Hip Arthroplasty (C-THA) for young, active patients. While concerns over metal-on-metal (MoM) bearings have reduced utilisation, contemporary data on well-performing devices such as the Birmingham Hip Resurfacing (BHR) demonstrate favourable medium- to long-term outcomes in appropriately selected patients, and novel ceramic-on-ceramic (CoC) resurfacing systems are emerging. This updated meta-analysis synthesises current evidence on 10-year survival, cumulative revision, and functional outcomes of R-THA in patients under 55 years of age. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines [1]. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register (January 2015 – February 2026) for studies reporting ≥ 10-year follow-up of R-THA in patients < 55 years of age or containing an extractable subgroup for this population. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) [2] for cohort studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool for the single randomised trial. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian–Laird) was performed on logit-transformed proportions of implant survival and all-cause revision. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses excluded recalled implants (Durom). The certainty of evidence was considered using the GRADE framework [3]. Results Eleven studies comprising R-THA cohorts in young active patients met the inclusion criteria for quantitative synthesis; the sample is dominated by Birmingham Hip Resurfacing (BHR) cohorts and by the large-registry data from the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry (AOANJRR) [4], so the pooled estimates reflect well-performing BHR in selected patients treated at experienced centres rather than resurfacing arthroplasty as a class. The primary, time-dependent outcome—pooled 10-year Kaplan–Meier implant survival—was 95.0% (95% CI 94.4–95.6%; I² = 7.4%), corresponding to a cumulative percent revision of approximately 5.0% at 10 years. The pooled all-cause proportion of hips revised during study follow-up, a non-time-adjusted descriptor that is sensitive to follow-up length and is therefore interpreted only as supplementary, was 6.3% (95% CI 4.8–8.3%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 80.8%) driven largely by implant design. Sensitivity analysis restricted to BHR devices reduced heterogeneity considerably. The weighted mean Harris Hip Score was 93.3 points, reported descriptively only and subject to ceiling effects. Novel ceramic-on-ceramic hybrid resurfacing (ReCerf) has reported 5-year survival of 98.0% in an international multicentre cohort [5]; these data are short-term and are discussed as emerging evidence only. Conclusions In appropriately selected young active patients treated at experienced centres, R-THA—particularly the BHR—provides durable medium- to long-term survivorship and good functional outcomes. These findings predominantly reflect the BHR rather than resurfacing arthroplasty as a class. Large registry data indicate that selected contemporary C-THA constructs with crosslinked-polyethylene or ceramic-on-ceramic bearings achieve superior all-cause cumulative revision outcomes compared with the BHR in the same target population, and do so without jurisdiction-specific metal-ion surveillance [4]. R-THA should therefore be offered, after balanced counselling, as one reasonable option among several to informed, appropriately selected patients, and performed in experienced centres. Emerging ceramic-on-ceramic systems are promising but require long-term confirmatory data before their role can be defined.

papers.title: Surgical treatment of an extensive acetabular defect in a patient with aseptic instability of a total hip arthroplasty: a clinical case and updated literature review
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to demonstrate, using a clinical example, the possibility of one-stage revision hip arthroplasty with a custom 3D-printed acetabular implant for an extensive acetabular defect with pelvic discontinuity, and to review recent literature on this topic. We report a 45-year-old female patient with multiple prior hip surgeries (reconstructive procedures in childhood; primary and revision arthroplasties in 1991, 1998, 2001 and 2012) who presented in 2019 with aseptic instability of the right total hip arthroplasty and a Paprosky type IIIB acetabular defect. One-stage revision arthroplasty was performed using a custom triflange acetabular component designed from CT data and manufactured from titanium powder using direct metal laser sintering (DMLS). The Harris Hip Score improved from 21 points preoperatively to 82 points at 6 months; the WOMAC score decreased from 73 to 15 points over the same period. No early postoperative complications occurred; mild residual limp related to scarring and gluteal muscle atrophy persisted. An updated review of the 2018–2026 literature confirms that custom additively manufactured implants remain an effective option for restoring limb support and hip function in extensive acetabular defects and pelvic discontinuity, although dislocation, nerve injury and infection remain relevant risks requiring further refinement of planning, fixation and stability strategies.

papers.title: Stochastic modeling for uncertainty quantification in COVID-19 dynamics using Euler Maruyama approximation
papers.abstract: We propose a stochastic extension of a compartmental epidemiological model for COVID-19 to describe the transmission dynamics in Bogotá, Colombia. To account for intrinsic variability in infection, incubation, recovery, and vaccination processes, random perturbations are incorporated into key model parameters. The resulting system of stochastic differential equations is approximated using the Euler-Maruyama method, enabling likelihood-based parameter estimation. We derive an extended basic reproduction number, along with its associated uncertainty, providing a statistically grounded measure of epidemic potential under varying conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully captures the variability observed in the epidemiological data and highlights the importance of accounting for parameter uncertainty in public health decision-making. The model is statistically tractable, computationally efficient, and adaptable to other infectious diseases and urban settings. Possible extensions include incorporating reinfection dynamics, integrating additional data sources, and using Bayesian inference to enhance uncertainty quantification.

summary_zh.motivation: 为刻画COVID-19传播中的内在随机性并量化参数不确定性。
summary_zh.method: 在分室模型参数中引入随机扰动，用Euler-Maruyama方法近似随机微分方程并做似然估计。
summary_zh.result: 模型能复现Bogotá疫情数据的波动，并给出基本再生数及其不确定性。
summary_zh.validation: 基于实际流行病学数据的数值模拟验证。

summary_en.motivation: To capture intrinsic randomness in COVID-19 transmission and quantify parameter uncertainty for public health decisions.
summary_en.method: Random perturbations are added to compartmental model parameters, and the resulting stochastic differential equations are approximated via the Euler-Maruyama scheme with likelihood-based estimation.
summary_en.result: The framework reproduces observed variability in Bogotá epidemiological data and yields an extended basic reproduction number with associated uncertainty.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation against real epidemiological data from Bogotá.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification propagation in FNG HCPB-tritium breeding module using OpenMC-SANDY workflow
papers.abstract: Nuclear data (ND) uncertainty quantification (UQ) supports the establishment of safety margins for fusion neutronic designs. This study applies an open-source, stochastic UQ workflow — coupling the continuous-energy Monte Carlo transport code OpenMC with the SANDY nuclear-data sampling toolkit — to the Frascati Neutron Generator (FNG) Helium-Cooled Pebble Bed (HCPB) Tritium Breeding Module (TBM) mock-up benchmark. ENDF/B-VIII.0 and JEFF-3.3 serve as the transport base libraries, with SANDY generating 400 random samples from its covariance evaluation to propagate within-library ND uncertainty to the Tritium Production Rate ( T P R ) in the L i 2 C O 3 detector pellets and to activation reaction rates at increasing shielding depth. A prior sensitivity screening identified the 9 ⁢ B e ⁡ ( 𝑛 , t o t a l ) and ( 𝑛 , 2 ⁢ 𝑛 ) channels and 6 ⁢ L i ⁡ ( 𝑛 , 𝛼 ) ⁢ t as the leading contributors. 9 ⁢ B e cross-section uncertainty dominates the computational variance. The ND contribution to calculated T P R is approximately 4% ( 2 ⁢ 𝜎 coverage), with per-run Monte Carlo statistical error held below 0.5%. Measured TPR carries an experimental uncertainty of approximately 7.8% ( 2 ⁢ 𝜎 ). Rather than summing these into a single figure, calculation and measurement are compared as C/E ratios per pellet stack, which show reasonable agreement with the uncertainty band. A spatial gradient in ND uncertainty is observed, the calculated spread widening from 2 – 3 % at the front stack to 3 – 5 % at the rear. Calculated activation and TPR profiles show reasonable agreement with experiment, with the exception of a consistent underprediction of low-energy monitors, most notably 1 9 7 ⁢ A u ⁡ ( 𝑛 , 𝛾 ) . It is attributed to an under-moderated calculated flux at depth, implicating the thermal-scattering ( 𝑆 ⁡ ( 𝛼 , 𝛽 ) ) and elastic-scattering data of the beryllium multiplier — rather than to the Au evaluation itself, and is identified for further investigation on that basis. Because the same effect implies that parasitic low-energy capture may be underestimated in the model, its impact on the tritium breeding ratio (TBR) is not assumed to be conservative; the directional effect is quantified directly rather than asserted.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文是聚变中子学中的核数据不确定性传播工作流，与用户关注的FEA代理模型、植入物力学无直接关系，仅可作为UQ方法论的背景参考。
llm.why_not_core: This paper performs nuclear-data uncertainty propagation in a fusion neutronics benchmark and contains no FEA surrogate modelling, no solid-mechanics or implant biomechanics context, and no design optimization under constraints.

summary_zh.motivation: 为聚变中子学设计建立安全裕度，需要量化核数据不确定性对氚增殖率的影响。
summary_zh.method: 耦合OpenMC连续能量蒙特卡洛输运与SANDY核数据采样工具，对FNG HCPB氚增殖模块基准生成400个随机样本进行不确定性传播。
summary_zh.result: 9Be截面不确定性主导计算方差，氚增殖率核数据贡献约4%（2σ），不确定度随屏蔽深度从前端2–3%增至后端3–5%。
summary_zh.validation: 以FNG基准实验测量的氚增殖率和活化率作为参照，用C/E比值逐层对比计算与实验的不确定度带。

summary_en.motivation: Safety margins for fusion neutronic designs require quantifying how nuclear-data uncertainty propagates into tritium production predictions.
summary_en.method: An open-source stochastic workflow couples the OpenMC continuous-energy Monte Carlo transport code with the SANDY nuclear-data sampling toolkit, drawing 400 samples from covariance evaluations to propagate within-library uncertainty in the FNG HCPB tritium breeding module benchmark.
summary_en.result: 9Be cross-section uncertainty dominates the computational variance, the nuclear-data contribution to tritium production rate is about 4% at 2 sigma, and the uncertainty spread widens from 2-3% at the front stack to 3-5% at the rear.
summary_en.validation: Calculated tritium production and activation profiles are compared against FNG benchmark measurements through per-stack C/E ratios with their respective uncertainty bands.

papers.title: Research on real-time regulation of driver thermal comfort based on artificial intelligent and model predictive control

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将MPC与AI用于汽车座舱热舒适调节，与用户关注的RL/世界模型及工程仿真（FEA/植入物力学）方向关联很弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper applies model predictive control to automotive cabin thermal comfort and contains no reinforcement learning, world models, FEA/surrogate modeling, or biomechanical/implant context.

summary_zh.motivation: 提升汽车座舱乘员热舒适并降低空调能耗。
summary_zh.method: 结合人工智能预测模型与模型预测控制实时调节座舱热环境。
summary_zh.result: 实现热舒适与能耗的协同优化。
summary_zh.validation: 基于热环境仿真案例进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve occupant thermal comfort in vehicle cabins while reducing HVAC energy consumption.
summary_en.method: An AI-based thermal prediction model is integrated with model predictive control to regulate the cabin thermal environment in real time.
summary_en.result: The control scheme reportedly balances thermal comfort against energy use.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies on thermal-environment simulation cases rather than physical experiments.
